one_liner: Tiny R package exposing RomuTrio, xoshiro256+, lehmer64 and SplitMix64 as runif-style functions, about 20x faster than R's runif().
what_it_does: Adds four small-state 64-bit PRNGs to R, each with set_seed_*, get_state_*/set_state_* (state as raw bytes), runif1_* (one draw) and runif_*(n, min, max) (vector of doubles); xoshiro256+ also gets jump and long_jump. It is a separate set of generators with their own process-wide state, not an RNGkind plug-in, so set.seed() and the rest of R's distribution functions are unaffected. Each generator is one 110-230 line C file under src/ that wraps the published reference algorithm in R glue.
how_it_is_fast: Each runif_* call runs one tight C loop that steps the generator inline and converts the top 53 bits to a double with (x >> 11) * 0x1.0p-53, writing straight into a freshly allocated REALSXP. The generators themselves are cheap: RomuTrio is a multiply plus two subtract-rotates, xoshiro256+ is xor/shift/rotate, lehmer64 is one 128-bit multiply (unsigned __int128), SplitMix64 is an add plus two xorshift-multiplies. The speedup is mostly avoided per-value overhead in R's runif path rather than a novel generator technique.
when_to_use: R code that draws millions of plain U(min, max) doubles in a hot loop and does not need set.seed() reproducibility through R's own RNG machinery.
You need to save and restore generator state exactly (get_state_*/set_state_* as raw vectors) or skip ahead 2^128/2^192 steps with jump_xoshiro256p/long_jump_xoshiro256p.
You want a readable reference of how to bind a small C PRNG to R's .Call interface with state save/restore.
Linux or macOS 64-bit R builds, where all four generators compile (lehmer64 needs unsigned __int128).
when_not_to_use: C++ projects: the files add only R glue (R.h/Rinternals.h, SEXP returns, global state); take the generators from their reference sources or a catalogued C++ library instead.
You need normals, integers, sampling or other distributions: only uniform doubles are provided (dqrng covers rnorm and sample.int).
Windows R builds that need lehmer64: it is compiled out under _WIN32 and runif_lehmer64 prints a message and returns a single 0 instead of n values.

Production or packaged work: lifecycle badge says experimental, 11 commits, last code change September 2020, install is from GitHub only per the README, and issue #1 (Windows i386 build failure) has no maintainer reply.
Parallel or multi-stream use: each generator has exactly one global stream per process, with no per-object state.

integration.dependencies: R (built via R CMD INSTALL / remotes::install_github); testthat suggested for tests
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler accepted by R's build tools; lehmer64 needs unsigned __int128 (64-bit GCC or Clang). R version minimum not documented.
integration.platforms: Any 64-bit R build for xoshiro256+, RomuTrio and SplitMix64; lehmer64 disabled on Windows
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe: each generator keeps its state in a file-scope static (or global) variable shared by every caller in the process.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — runif_*(n, min, max) mirrors runif's signature, but min/max are read as scalars (only the first element is used, unlike runif's recycling), seeding goes through set_seed_* rather than set.seed(), and the streams differ from Mersenne-Twister.

gotchas: Licensing is mixed despite the package's MIT label: romutrio.c carries Mark Overton's Apache-2.0 header and xoshiro256p.c/splitmix64.c carry Blackman/Vigna CC0 headers; vendoring romutrio.c brings Apache-2.0 obligations.

Generators are seeded once in .onLoad from stats::runif, so results are reproducible only if you call the package's set_seed_* (or set.seed() before the package loads); forked workers such as parallel::mclapply would start from copies of the same state unless reseeded or jumped (inferred from the global state in the C code).
The double conversion maps 53 bits to [0, 1), so an exact 0 (or min) is a possible output.
romutrio.c does arithmetic on void* when copying state (pbytes + 8), a GNU extension; porting it to strict C or C++ needs a cast to unsigned char*.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick dqrng over this for almost any R use: it is a header-only C++ library and R package with xoshiro256++/PCG64, fast rnorm and sample.int, and active maintenance. miranda is only the better pick if you specifically want RomuTrio or lehmer64 behind a runif-like call; for C++ code use the reference generators directly (Romu, testingRNG's lehmer64) or a SIMD sibling such as simdrng.
verified_claims_summary: README bench::mark of 1e6 uniform doubles: R's runif(N) (default Mersenne-Twister) sits at about 30 ms, while non-GC iterations of runif_romutrio and runif_xoshiro256p cluster near 1.5 ms, lehmer64 near 1.7 ms and splitmix64 near 2.5 ms (about 12x-20x, values read off a log-axis beeswarm, derived from page data); iterations that triggered garbage collection took 5-13 ms. No CPU, R version, compiler or flags are given, and the gap measures R's runif call path against an inlined C loop, not generator against generator in C++.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022 (last code change September 2020, then a README typo fix); MIT package licence with Apache-2.0 and CC0 file headers, and the C cores are small enough to vendor, but they offer nothing over the upstream reference sources for C++ users.
